sentence: a sanitized NCCL receipt on three cards at Gen2 x16 behind PLX switches measures 6.63–6.68 GB/s host-staged copy [[readmemd]] (T2)
problem: Configuration is right (three cards, Gen2 x16, two PLX PEX 8747 switches, sanitized receipt) but the magnitude is not. The note's host-staged copy measurement is cuMemcpyPeer at 256 MiB = 6.21–6.30 GB/s; 6.68 GB/s is the note's single-card D2H reference (a different configuration, not a host-staged inter-card copy), and 6.63 GB/s appears nowhere in this note — it is the ocl_pcie_bw figure from physical-modsmd / pcie-subsystemmd on a different rig. The report's own Source Tensions section already uses the correct 6.21–6.30 GB/s figure for this rig, so §1 is internally inconsistent.
evidence: readmemd Results table: `cuMemcpyPeer`, 256 MiB | 6.21–6.30 GB/s (single-card D2H: 6.68 GB/s). No 6.63 anywhere in the note.
suggested_fix: Change the number to 6.21–6.30 GB/s host-staged copy (cuMemcpyPeer) against a 6.68 GB/s single-card D2H reference. If the 6.63–6.67 figure is wanted, cite [[physical-modsmd]] or [[pcie-subsystemmd]] and label it ocl_pcie_bw on a four-card rig, not the three-card NCCL receipt.

sentence: At Gen2 x16, NCCL reaches 3.69–4.24 GB/s busbw against a 6.63–6.68 GB/s one-way rate — 53–64% of the link [[readmemd]] (T2/T4)
problem: The busbw half is supported (3.69 / 3.85 / 4.24 GB/s). The one-way-rate half is not: the note's one-way figures are 6.68 GB/s (single-card D2H reference) and 6.21–6.30 GB/s (cuMemcpyPeer host-staged copy); 6.63 GB/s is absent. The derived efficiency band is also off at the low end — 3.69/6.68 = 55.2%, so the band is 55–64%, not 53–64%.
evidence: readmemd: busbw 3.69 GB/s (same-switch pair), 3.85 GB/s (cross-switch pair), 4.24 GB/s (all three); cuMemcpyPeer 6.21–6.30 GB/s; D2H reference 6.68 GB/s.
suggested_fix: Use 6.68 GB/s (single-card D2H reference) as the one-way rate and 55–64% as the efficiency band; or use 6.21–6.30 GB/s and 59–68%. Drop the 6.63 lower bound, which is not in this note.

sentence: What remains is the bubble: (5−1)/32 = 12.5% for 1F1B at 32 micro-batches, ~4.2% for zero-bubble schedules, and under 4.5% measured for RoundPipe with asynchronous optimizer updates [[efficient-training-on-multiple-consumer-gpus-with]] (T2/T3)
problem: The RoundPipe clause is supported ('driving the absolute bubble ratio down to below 4.5%'). The ~4.2% zero-bubble figure is not in this note — it mentions Zero-Bubble schedules only qualitatively — and belongs to [[zero-bubble-pipeline-parallelism]] ('bubble size is reduced to a third of 1F1B's size', i.e. 12.5%/3 ≈ 4.2%). The 1F1B figure also conflicts with this note's own formula: the note gives the bubble as (S−1)/(M+S−1), which at S=5, M=32 is 11.1%, not (S−1)/M = 12.5%.
evidence: RoundPipe note: 'pipeline bubble of (S−1)/(M+S−1)'; 'RoundPipe with asynchronous optimizer updates ... driving the absolute bubble ratio down to below 4.5%'. No 4.2% anywhere; zero-bubble note: 'bubble size is reduced to a third of 1F1B's size'.
suggested_fix: Split the citation: keep [[efficient-training-on-multiple-consumer-gpus-with]] for the <4.5% RoundPipe figure and add [[zero-bubble-pipeline-parallelism]] for the ~4.2% ZB-H1 figure, or delete the zero-bubble clause.
